Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

what have you got to do with …? phrase

also what do you have to do with him?, what business is it of yours?, what is he to you?, what do you care about

classical

Ter. Eun. 3.3.4: Quid tibi cum illā? (Lewis & Short), s.v. tum
Sen. Ep. 15.10: quid tibi cum cēterīs?

Quid tibi cum (illō)?

question without a verb: quid with the dative of the person and cum with the ablative

what have you to do with him?

The dative is the person asked, cum the person or thing he has dealings with; est is left out.

Other words

  • Quid tibi reī est cum (illō)? — what business have you with him?

    reī, partitive genitive; Plautus has commercī in the same frame · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 4.4.4: quid tibi mēcum est commercī, senex? (Lewis & Short), s.v. commercium; Traupman 100

Examples

  • quid tibi cum cēterīs? tē ipse antecessistī

    what do you care about the others? you’ve beaten yourselfSen. Ep. 15.10

See also concern.
